entities.summary: The Støre Cabinet is the incumbent government of the Kingdom of Norway, headed by Labour Party leader Jonas Gahr Støre as Prime Minister. The government was appointed by King Harald V on 14 October 2021, following the parliamentary election on 13 September, consisting of the Labour Party (Ap) and the Centre Party (Sp) as a minority government. On 30 January 2025, the Centre Party withdrew from government over disagreements over the implementation of three directives in the European Union's fourth energy package. The one-party minority cabinet won re-election at the 2025 parliamentary election.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Støre Cabinet's minority government was marked by its handling of the European Union's fourth energy package, with the Centre Party's withdrawal in January 2025 leading to a re-election victory for the Labour Party-led cabinet. This event highlights the challenges faced by Norway's government in navigating EU policies and their impact on domestic politics.
